rationale: The pre-vote-disabled receipt separates the two gates the earlier negative result left entangled, so the account of why uniform configurations keep the separation can now name the gate that does the work instead of the combination. Every trial formed the higher-term candidacy the previous run could not, and no trial produced an overlap, which puts the separation on the peers' known-leader refusal together with their own heartbeat timers and makes pre-vote an additional gate that prevents the candidacy from forming at all. This submission appends that interpretation, corrects the knowledge entry under its existing id with the changed premise and its recorded use, and marks the question answered.

knowledge.statement: Uniformly configured clusters keep a cut-off leader's confirmation window ahead of any competing election, and the gate that does it is the peers' refusal to vote while they still have the leader in view: a node with a known leader rejects a vote request from any other candidate before comparing terms, and that knowledge lapses no earlier than its own heartbeat timer, which ValidateConfig keeps at or above the leader's lease. Pre-vote is a second, additional gate rather than the necessary one: with pre-vote enabled an isolated node never raises its term, and with pre-vote disabled it does raise its term and still cannot collect a vote before the lease expires, which is what the pre-vote-disabled run measured.
knowledge.conditions: Nodes sharing their timer settings; ValidateConfig's per-node relation LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout holding; the candidate isolated from the leader and from a majority of voters. The additional pre-vote gate applies when pre-vote is enabled, which is the captured default.
knowledge.changed_premise: The original statement said two gates keep the separation and that the run could not attribute it to either alone. The pre-vote-disabled run shows the higher-term candidacy forming in every trial while the separation still held, so the statement now distinguishes the gate that produces the separation (a peer that still has the leader in view refuses the vote request before comparing terms, and that view lapses no earlier than the peer's own heartbeat timer, which with shared settings is at least the leader's lease) from the additional gate (with pre-vote enabled the candidacy does not form at all). The behaviour described is a correction of attribution, not of the observations.

interpretations.rationale: Retained execution (check 17133140c8064f01b7884e490ec6bc02, exit 0, tests_passed, 52 parsed events, 0 parse errors; twelve hand-built four-node clusters with identical 50ms settings and PreVoteDisabled set on every node). Comparison 0, which predicted that a live higher-term candidacy would let a confirmation overlap a competing election, came back violated and complete, with all twelve trials as valid witnesses: no trial produced a competing leader during the confirmation window and none produced a confirmation after one. The trials nevertheless did produce what they were built to force: preexisting_candidate is true in all twelve, and the isolated voter sat at terms three to five against a leader at two or three, so unlike the previous run a real, higher-term candidacy was alive throughout the window. The confirmations ended at the leader's lease in every trial (47-59ms, seventeen to twenty confirmations each) and the leader stepped down in every trial. Together with the earlier run - where pre-vote kept the isolated voter at the leader's own term - the two receipts separate the gates: pre-vote prevents an isolated node from raising its term at all, and it is the peers' known-leader refusal, released only when their own heartbeat timers expire, that keeps the separation when a candidacy does exist. That is consistent with the mechanism entry, which is corrected in this submission to say so, and it leaves the mixed-timer finding as the only path into the defect, now for the precise reason that only a node whose own timer is shorter than the leader's lease can get ahead of it.

knowledge.assertion: The two gates named there were exercised together by the earlier run; this run exercises the pre-vote-disabled branch and separates their roles.

counterevidence: Pre-vote is disabled in this run, so the configuration is legal but not the captured default; the default case is the earlier run, which is what the two receipts are compared for.
The candidacy was produced by isolating one voter rather than by catching a live campaign in a healthy cluster, so the history is constructed even though the candidacy itself is real.
No application read is served, so what is measured is the coexistence of a confirmation with a competing leader rather than a delivered value.
One timer pair (50ms everywhere) and one cluster shape; a cluster whose peers have longer timers than the leader's lease is the mixed case, covered separately.
limitations: One cluster shape (three voters plus one nonvoter, quorum two) in one process with in-memory transports.
The isolated voter was given up to three seconds to campaign; longer histories were not tried.
The negative result spans two configurations (pre-vote on and off) but only one set of timer values.
